## Summary (Ask Bunkankun 聞分館君)

A short single-juan dhāraṇī-sūtra translated at the Sòng 譯經院 by [施護](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E6%96%BD%E8%AD%B7) Shīhù (*Dānapāla*, d. 1017). CANWWW restores the Sanskrit title as *Jñānolkā-nāma-dhāraṇī-sarvadurgati-pariśodhanī(sūtra)* — exactly the same Sanskrit base text underlying [KR6j0629](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6j/KR6j0629) (T1397) by [提雲般若](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E6%8F%90%E9%9B%B2%E8%88%AC%E8%8B%A5) Devaprajñā some three centuries earlier. The Sòng version is a fresh translation of the same Indian *vidyā*. CANWWW alt-title 智光滅業障經.

**Abstract**

The Buddha is in the *Sun-and-Moon Devaputra*'s palace (日月天子宮 — i.e. the Sūrya/Candra-deva palace), with multiple Tathāgatas present: *Zhìguāng* 智光 (Skt. *Jñāna-prabha* / *Jñānolkā*), *Zhēnshí* 真實, *Jīnguāngjù* 金光聚, *Shēnshēn shēngwáng* 甚深聲王, *Fènnù* 忿怒, *Bǎoyuè* 寶月; together with the bodhisattvas Samantabhadra, Mañjuśrī, *Chídìwáng* 持地王, *Vajrapāṇi*, and others. The Buddha pronounces the *Jñānolkā-dhāraṇī*, which expunges all karmic obstacles and purifies beings of all unwholesome destinies. The Sanskrit *Jñānolkā-nāma-dhāraṇī* survives in Sanskrit manuscript and in Tibetan canonical translation. Recorded in the *Dàzhōngxiángfú fǎbǎo lù*; Nanjio N0835. The dating window 982–1017 covers Shīhù's translation career at the Sòng 譯經院.
